headline: BEANS FLAT, DIESEL AT $6.50, CRUDE BREAKS ON IRAN THAW
lead: Soybeans sit at $13.10, off a penny and a half, still waiting on Xi. Meanwhile diesel crossed $6.50 a gallon this weekend, a record, while crude fell to $92.97 on Iran diplomacy hopes: two energy stories moving in opposite directions on the same headline.
teaser: Diesel hit a record $6.50 a gallon even as crude fell on Iran talk, a split that's already in your harvest budget.

one_number.unit: tankers crossing Strait of Hormuz this weekend
one_number.context: Versus 35 tankers a normal weekend; traffic keeps thinning even as crude falls on diplomacy hopes, a split worth watching.

action: Diesel at $6.50/gallon: lock harvest fuel needs now, don't wait for crude's Iran-talk dip to reach the pump.

sections.title: Diesel Record, Crude Breaks
sections.body:
- Crude fell 1.1% to **$92.97** on hopes for an Iran diplomatic deal, even as retail diesel hit a record $6.50 a gallon this weekend.
- Oilprice.com reports Hormuz tanker traffic thinned to just a dozen vessels this weekend versus a normal 35, the freight story now bigger than the crude story.
sections.so_what: Crude and diesel are decoupled; input costs aren't falling with the crude tape.

sections.title: Beans Wait On Xi
sections.body:
- Soybeans held **$13.10**, basically flat, after Friday's fund liquidation and pre-weekend profit-taking that Feedstuffs flagged as traders positioning ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting.
- No fresh purchase confirmation since Friday; the board is pricing a summit outcome that hasn't happened yet.
sections.so_what: The whole complex is a summit bet now, not a fundamentals trade.

outside_the_pit.title: August Feeder Placements Drop To Record Low
outside_the_pit.body: Drovers reports August cattle placements into feedlots fell to a record low as screwworm-driven border limits keep tightening feeder supply into fall.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above last week's mark keeps the Belt on schedule.
Trump-Xi meeting; a confirmed bean purchase over 1 MMT is the number that moves $13.10.
Diesel above $6.50/gallon; a close above $6.75 forces harvest budgets to reprice again.

daily_quote.text: The worst thing about being wrong is the lesson you learn.

source_summary: CME/CBOT settlement data, USDA, Agri-Pulse, Feedstuffs, Drovers, Oilprice.com, AgWeb
